title: Depth=11 fine bracket
description: Changed DEPTH from 10 to 11 to test the gap between depth=10 (winner) and depth=12 (confounded loser); crashed with CUDA OOM at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128.
reflection: DEPTH=11 is not actually a clean midpoint: model_dim = ceil(depth*64/128)*128 means depth=10 gives model_dim=640 (5 heads) but depth=11 jumps straight to model_dim=768 (6 heads) -- the same width as depth=12, just with one extra layer. So DEPTH=11 is strictly bigger than DEPTH=12, not a bracket point between 10 and 12, and it OOM'd even worse than depth=12 did. Abandoning after one crash rather than retrying with a reduced batch size, since that would just reproduce the same batch-size confound that already made the depth=12 result ambiguous, on a config that's unlikely to beat depth=10 anyway. Key takeaway for the group: because of the HEAD_DIM rounding in build_model_config, model_dim only takes discrete values as DEPTH increases (640 at depth 8-10, 768 at depth 11-12), so the real depth/width bracket to test next is DEPTH=9 (model_dim=640, same width as 10, one fewer layer) or exploring HEAD_DIM directly to get finer-grained width control.
